Basket still on belt: projected alignment lacked insertion depth. Reopen right, lower to shoulder and advance 6 cm while following conveyor; keep left hovering.
Retract left slightly from IK limit. Right inserts farther around the visible curved handle, lowers slightly and closes while tracking drift.
Use submillimeter left retreat from near-limit configuration after rejection. Continue right insertion and close around handle.
Finish right closure at deeper handle contact, then test lift while no longer following belt. Left tracks the cup laterally without picking yet.

Close left around matched cup while tracking. Keep right closed and begin correcting basket's sideways tilt, bringing basket nearer center without crossing arms.
Test left cup retention by lifting and retracting, maintaining closure. Continue right rotation toward an upward-facing basket and move its opening toward center.
Cup remained on belt. Reopen left, descend deeper and tilt fingers forward to grasp body without overextending. Right maintains lifted basket and finishes leveling.
Descend an additional 1.5 cm around cup body, close while tracking belt. Hold lifted, leveled basket steady with right.
Cup is visibly contacted between left jaws. Keep closed and lift 10 cm with slight retreat to verify retention; right holds basket steady.
Cup slipped from shallow contact. Reopen and descend substantially farther around the body, tracking near the shared center while staying separated from right arm.
Now at substantial cup-body depth. Close and make a small retention lift; move held basket slightly right to clear cup from its outer wall.
After IK interruption, retract left toward its own workspace using small increments while holding cup and gaining lift; maintain right basket grasp.

Use submillimeter horizontal inward increments only to recover continuity near the left extension limit; no compensation for rejected moves.
Both objects slipped during contact. Withdraw left to its side; right approaches the now-rightward cup with vertical jaw separation for a side grasp.
Lower right jaws to the lying cup rather than above it, then close. Reverse left's last path carefully to recover the intended elbow configuration.
Correct right grasp deeper and lower around the lying cup while matching conveyor motion. Continue tiny left reverse-path corrections, avoiding configuration jumps.
Test right cup grasp with a small inward lift. Continue very small left reverse-path corrections near its singular configuration; do not advance across the workspace.
Right grasp missed laterally: use head and wrist views to align farther right and lower at the moving cup body, then close. Left continues slow configuration recovery.
Finish closing right around visibly centered cup and test a 3 cm lift. Left gently increases forward wrist tilt and retreats to regain elbow-up reach margin.

Retry right clearance and downward reorientation at less than half increments after zero-step continuity rejection.
Continue right top-down approach above moving cup, open jaws; small left reverse wrist rotations recover prior configuration without translating farther across center.
Finish a near-downward right orientation while following cup laterally, without advancing too far past it. Left continues slow reverse wrist recovery.
Use wrist view to center lying cup under right downward jaws, then close while tracking. Continue smooth left reverse wrist motion away from its near-straight configuration.

Finish closure without chasing, then perform a short inward lift to determine from RGB whether the cup is actually retained.
